name: Tanuki Transplanter
oracle_text:
Whenever this creature or equipped creature attacks, add an amount of {G} equal to its power. Until end of turn, you don't lose this mana as steps and phases end.
Reconfigure {3} ({3}: Attach to target creature you control; or unattach from a creature. Reconfigure only as a sorcery. While attached, this isn't a creature.)
blocked_sentences: Until end of turn, you don't lose this mana as steps and phases end.

needs.what: Mana that survives the end of a step or phase -- the Upwelling / Kruphix / Omnath effect, printed here as a rider on one add_mana rather than as a standing static. Concretely: ManaPool (src/automtg/engine/mana.py) needs to carry persistence pip by pip alongside its existing `tags` provenance list, so that `ManaPool.clear()` keeps the marked pips instead of zeroing `amounts`, plus a turn-boundary sweep that does empty them (rule 500.4 still applies at cleanup, and "until end of turn" means the exemption expires there). Then an authoring spelling: either a `persists_until_end_of_turn` key on the `add_mana` op marking only the mana that op produced, or a player-wide entry in `static_effects` for the cards that print the standing version -- this card needs the per-add_mana form, because only the mana this trigger made is exempt.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `add_mana` and `add_mana_per` are the only ops that put mana in a pool and neither has any key touching its lifetime -- op_options for `add_mana` is amount/in_commander_identity/mana/player/reflecting/split, and op_add_mana (engine/effects/ops_mana.py) simply calls `mana_pool.add_tuple`. `state.empty_all_mana_pools` calls `ManaPool.clear()`, which unconditionally replaces `amounts` with zeros and `tags` with empty lists; it is called from turn.py at every step/phase boundary and from sba.py, and there is no flag, tag or per-pip field it consults. `mana_restriction` is the nearest thing in the DSL that qualifies mana, but it is a spend-only-on narrowing, and the loader raises "'mana_restriction' needs 'is_mana_ability'" -- this is a triggered ability that uses the stack, not a mana ability. `delayed_trigger` and `delay` cannot stand in either: they schedule effects at a later step, and by then the pool has already been cleared, so re-adding mana there would be a different card that makes mana twice. Dropping the sentence leaves a Tanuki Transplanter whose mana vanishes the instant the declare-attackers step ends, which is the whole point of the card -- the ramp is meant to be spendable in the postcombat main phase.
